Ask for an app PIN (and optionally your fingerprint) when opening MailCtrl. While locked, your drafts stay encrypted with the PIN and the recent-apps screen hides your mail.
At least %1$d digits, different from your phone\'s PIN.

A fingerprint was added or removed. Unlock with your PIN, then turn fingerprint unlock on again.
Couldn\'t unlock with your fingerprint. Use your PIN.
Only strong biometrics such as your fingerprint, checked by the phone\'s secure hardware. The PIN is still needed after a restart and every 72 hours.
Confirm it\'s you to see your mail
Set up a fingerprint on this phone first

The PIN can\'t be recovered. Confirm it\'s you with your phone\'s own screen lock to turn the app lock off. Drafts encrypted with the old PIN are deleted, and accounts whose password was sealed with it ask for their password again. Your mail stays on your servers.

The PIN can\'t be recovered, and this phone has no screen lock to confirm it\'s you. To start over, clear MailCtrl\'s storage in Android\'s settings and add your accounts again (your mail stays on your servers).
The PINs didn\'t match. Start again.
Enter your PIN. It\'s needed after a restart and every 72 hours.

Accounts that are off are never checked in the background.
Sound, vibration and pop-ups, in Android\'s settings
Unrestricted lets Android run checks on time even while the phone sleeps. It costs very little: a check is one short connection per account.
Android may delay checks while the phone sleeps. Tap to allow MailCtrl to run unrestricted.

Android can delay background checks to save battery. With ntfy, whatever watches your mail (for example goimapnotify on your server) wakes MailCtrl the moment mail arrives; MailCtrl then checks and notifies you. The README shows how.
MailCtrl checks your inboxes itself, now and then, and tells you about new mail. Nothing goes through Google or any other push service.
Android can cut ntfy\'s connection while the phone sleeps, so wake-ups arrive late. Tap to open ntfy\'s App info and set Battery to Unrestricted.
Instant notifications come only through the ntfy app. Install it, then turn on Instant with ntfy. Background checks work without it.
Android blocks MailCtrl\'s notifications. Tap to allow them.
Your server wakes MailCtrl through the ntfy app when mail arrives
ntfy couldn\'t register MailCtrl (%1$s). Open ntfy once, then turn this on again.
Needs the ntfy app, which isn\'t installed
On. Give your mail watcher the address below
Posts to the push address, like your mail watcher will, so MailCtrl checks straight away
Couldn\'t reach the push address. Is your ntfy server reachable from this phone?
Sent. “Last wake-up” updates when it arrives.
ntfy temporarily unavailable: its server can\'t be reached. Your address stays the same, and background checks keep running.
Waiting for ntfy to give an address…
The password is needed again. Tap to enter it.
Encrypted with the phone\'s hardware key, so notifications work while locked
Sealed with your PIN: nothing can sign in while MailCtrl is locked
MailCtrl has no analytics or tracking. It only connects to your own mail servers.

Notifications are on, so background checks can sign in while MailCtrl is locked: passwords are then only encrypted with the phone\'s secure hardware, as without the app lock. Turn off notifications to seal them with your PIN too. MailCtrl has no analytics or tracking.
Pictures and content from the internet are blocked, so the sender can\'t see that you opened this.
Pictures loaded from the internet tell the sender when and where you opened a message. Pictures sent inside a message always show.
Searches on your mail server, so it finds everything, not just what\'s on the phone.
Try other words, or search another folder.
Not sent: %1$s. It\'s kept in your drafts.
Sent, but no copy could be put in the Sent folder

Providers with two-step sign-in want an app password here instead of your normal password: make one in your account\'s security settings. MailCtrl only signs in with a password (IMAP and SMTP); there\'s no sign-in through a web page.
Fill in both servers and their ports
Sign in with your address and password. MailCtrl talks to your mail server directly: no MailCtrl server, no tracking.
This provider doesn\'t let mail apps in (it has no IMAP), so it can\'t be added.
Check this account for new mail in the background
New password (leave empty to keep it)
Your password is encrypted with a key in the phone\'s secure hardware and only ever sent to your own mail servers.
Enter the address of your hydroxide or Proton Mail Bridge server below.
Proton Mail is read through hydroxide or Proton Mail Bridge running on your own server. Enter its address under Servers (over your VPN), and the password it gave you, not your Proton password.
Turn off for servers that do it themselves (otherwise sent mail shows up twice)
Your name (shown to people you write to)

With “None”, your password and mail travel unencrypted. Only use it for a server on your own network or over a VPN, such as hydroxide.

This account needs an app password, not your normal password. Make one in your account\'s security settings (two-step sign-in has to be on), then paste it here.
